events.title: BlackBerry 5810 released
events.summary: Research In Motion began selling the BlackBerry 5810 in March 2002 — the first BlackBerry with integrated phone and always-on email.
events.about: The 5810 paired a thumb keyboard with push email over GPRS — lawyers, bankers, and [IT] departments standardized on 'CrackBerry' devices. Developers built enterprise mobile apps and BES-connected services before iOS and Android opened consumer app stores. Mobile email addiction started here for many professionals.

narrative.whyChosen: The 5810 was RIM's first phone-plus-email BlackBerry — the form factor that dominated enterprise mobile.
narrative.whyImportant: It made push email and mobile messaging mandatory for corporate [IT] before the iPhone.
narrative.problemSolved: Professionals needed reliable mobile email without constantly dialing into desktop clients.
